**SECTION 9: SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT – CURRENT TERMS**

The Service Level Agreement specifies that the Service Desk response time target is 2 hours. Record status: current. This target applies to all priority-one (P1) and priority-two (P2) incidents logged by Harborview Adjusting Partners (HAP) staff through the Service Desk portal or telephone line, and remains in effect for the current contract term.

The current SLA was executed on 2025-01-15, replacing the prior agreement dated 2023-11-30. Key terms are summarized below:

| SLA Element | Current Term | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Service Desk response time target | 2 hours | Applies to P1 and P2 tickets during business hours (08:00–18:00 ET, Mon–Fri). |
| Incident resolution target | 8 business hours | Applies to P1 incidents; P2 incidents have a 24-business-hour target. |
| Escalation path | Tier 1 → Tier 2 → Vendor Management Office | Escalation after 1 missed response window. |
| Reporting cadence | Monthly performance report due by the 5th business day | Submitted by Service Desk lead to Vendor Management Office. |
| Review cycle | Quarterly service review meeting | Next scheduled review: 2025-09-18. |

Measurement of the response time target begins when the ticket is logged in the Service Desk system and ends when an analyst acknowledges the ticket and begins triage. Acknowledgment is confirmed by a timestamped note in the ticket history. The SLA does not include time spent waiting for HAP to provide additional information; such waiting periods are flagged as "on-hold" and excluded from the response calculation.

The current SLA term runs through 2026-01-14. Either party may propose amendments no later than 60 days before the renewal date. The Vendor Management Office is responsible for tracking SLA performance and for raising any recurring shortfalls during the quarterly service review.

**Section 6. Corrective Action Plan – Document Submission Completeness (Continued)**

The corrective action plan submitted by Harborview Adjusting Partners (HAP) on 2025-10-03 addressed both root causes as follows:

- **Field inspection photographs.** HAP revised its field inspection checklist (version 2.3, effective 2025-10-15) so that the photograph upload step is mandatory before the inspection report can be finalized. The prior checklist allowed the report to be submitted with a placeholder note if photographs were unavailable at the time of inspection. HAP also added a daily reconciliation report that flags any inspection file lacking the required photograph set. The 11 missing-photograph submissions were all from the period 2025-03-01 through 2025-06-30; no further instances have been identified in submissions dated on or after 2025-07-01.
- **Unsigned claimant statements.** HAP attributed the three unsigned statements to a workflow gap in its remote signing process. The adjuster would forward the claimant statement for electronic signature, but the system did not require confirmation that the signature was returned before the claim file was closed. HAP implemented a mandatory "signature verification" step in the claim closure workflow, effective 2025-10-20. The three affected files were reopened, the claimant statements were signed, and the files were reclosed on 2025-10-27.

The Vendor Management Office will verify sustained compliance during the Q1 2026 performance review. The Q4 2025 document submission completeness report is due from HAP by 2026-01-15.
